children: Nvidia's board is starting an independent investigation into reports that co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by an alleged foreign intelligence effort.

The investigation could put more pressure on Nvidia's stock, which is down 8.8% so far this month and down nearly 17% over the past three months, according to FactSet. The stock closed up 2.8% on Friday as stocks broadly recovered from Thursday's tech-driven rout.

Sunday's announcement by the board follows reports that Alice Huang or Huang Le, a Chinese citizen and top executive at a Singapore-based data center company who isn't related to Nvidia's CEO, was being scrutinized allegedly for helping the Chinese government obtain information about Nvidia's advanced AI chips.
The person had developed a close relationship with Nvidia's Huang, The Wall Street Journal reported, which cited a memo from Huang to employees.
"I owe my family and all of you an apology," the Journal reported the memo said.

"I was unfaithful to my wife," Huang's memo said. "My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry. ... I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it."

Nvidia's board in its own statement said it prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is "paramount to the interests of Nvidia and its shareholders." Although it said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information."

It said "Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it," adding that "The board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate."
The investigation will be overseen by a committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel. A spokesperson for Nvidia couldn't immediately be reached for comment.
Nvidia, which has a market cap of $4.5 trillion, reports third-quarter financial results on Nov. 17.
Corrections & Amplifications: Nvidia will report third-quarter earnings on Nov. 17. A previous version of this article incorrectly said it reports earnings on Thursday.
